Content: Photosynthetic activity can be measured using chloroplasts suspended in a buffered solution containing `text(DCPIP)`, a dye that can accept electrons from the electron transport chain of photosynthesis. Transfer of electrons to `text(DCPIP)` decreases the relative absorbance of a specific wavelength of light (`605` `text(nm)`) by a solution that contains the dye.

A buffered solution containing chloroplasts and `text(DCPIP)` was divided equally among `text(six)` identical samples. The samples were placed at various distances from a lamp, and then all samples were exposed to white light from the lamp for `60` `text(minutes)` at room temperature. Sample `3` was wrapped in foil to prevent any light from reaching the solution. At `20text(-minute)` intervals, the photosynthetic activity in `text(each sample)` was determined by measuring the relative absorbance of `605` `text(nm)` light.
